extraction.tool: Original native scan / closed-form edge alpha and foreground decontamination
extraction.ownership_guide_prompt: Use case: faithful historical illustration or ornament extraction. Edit the ORIGINAL supplied source region. Select only the left-facing EAGLE head and source-visible neck/chest, complete original gilded nimbus with its small pale beads, and both entire PALE BLUE wings. Keep the two wings and their nimbus/head together as the original winged symbol. Clear the purple niche ground, surrounding broad gold architectural arch, colored architecture and horizontal sill. The lower symbol is physically occluded by the sill: keep the original visible edge and do not invent a new body or neck. Preserve ALL pale beads of the halo even if individually separated by genuine tiny gaps; do not drop tiny pale details or pale feathers. Keep the entire selected original subject at its original proportions: every original fingertip, toe, petal fold, serration, thin stem, curl, feather, painted highlight and print hatching. Clear the unwanted page or flat painted background and every genuine opening between subject parts. Selected pale, gold, blue or white painted or engraved subject surfaces remain opaque. Remove neighboring unrelated subjects and printed page rules, lettering or captions. Preserve only source-visible parts, including original truncated ends; no invented hidden anatomy, new leaves, new tips, extended stalks, restored details or modern replacement artwork. Do not symmetrize, beautify, redraw, sharpen, stretch or compress the hand-drawn original. Fine natural antialiased contours without stepped polygon cuts or paper halos. Genuine transparent alpha outside and within the real openings, no rectangle or checkerboard paint. The enlarged source includes the COMPLETE long left feather tips; retain them down to their natural drawn ends. The big gilded ARCH outside the wings, and the pale PURPLE flat field between feathers, are architecture/background to remove. Keep the small complete GOLD NIMBUS around the head, all its cream beads and both original wings. The lion wings are pale yellow paint, the ox wings rose paint, and the eagle wings pale blue paint; follow the referenced subject's original wing boundaries. Do not retain any gilded arch fragments or broad purple background on those wings.
